bar, light header backdrop, the whole header (x 0 to 959) is painted mid grey #808080 with pure black "+", text, focus ring and hairline. It sits between the near-white Rail (#f5f5f7) and centre (#fff) and stops hard at the Shelf's edge, so the light app gets a heavy grey slab that looks unrelated to the rest of the screen. The cause is the scenario's 3:1 selected-surface-against-header requirement. bar, Project tab name inside its newly painted ground, scenario U441, step rest/selected (light-normal-tree-40-1280x800-head.png, dark-normal-agents-10-1280x800-head.png): the tab now paints a solid surface (#fff / #f5f5f7, dark #68686c / #141416), but the name's left edge is at x 16, the same as the tab's (measured live: tab x 16, text x 16). The "h" of "harness" touches the edge of the box, and the right side has a ragged, uneven pad. While the tab was unpainted this did not show; painting it exposes it, and the PR leaves U440's inset to later work, so main would ship broken-looking tabs. Change that would meet it: give .tab-name-button an inline pad of one space step on both sides (U440's inset) in the same PR, or leave the tab surfaces unpainted until U440 lands with them.

bar, dark selected tab, the selected tab's ground is #68686c (#707074 under hover), the brightest and loudest block on an otherwise #1c1c1e/#141416 screen. It is louder than the Rail's selected row and the Status Glyphs, and it holds #f5f5f7 text at only about 4.5:1, so it reads as washed out. The pastel Tab mark red #ffc0c0 drifts away from the Rail's error red. Change that would meet it: a selected ground one quiet step above the header (near the root --selected) with the hairline border marking the box, and the Tab mark in the root dark --red/--amber.

NOTE: Pressed handling through data-pressed and the root-Token reset for tooltip, menu and close dialog are sound. The scoped-Token approach keeps the Rail, Shelf and panes unchanged, as the committed captures show.

- `unfinished` (unfinished failed): Merge remote-tracking branch 'origin/main' into build/issue-1253; U378 make Workstream Agent add an explicit split button; U378 keep the stopped-Door add regression aligned with default nulls; U378 preserve vector and keyboard regressions for split add; U378 record split-add states and main design-check comparisons
- `critic` (critic rejected: The PR has no earlier critic findings to re-check: its only comment is a fix-run note.

Captured: tree-40, agents-10, first-run and conflict at 1280x800 and 1440x800, light and dark, on origin/main (956c027d) and head 32415fdc. The picker states use the same injected 20-Model list with 40-character labels that u378_rendered.test.ts uses. `window.__checks()` passes every Check on the head in the rest, hover and picker-open states. The head's picker fixes main's D2, D6, D7, D8 and D10 failures on `select.choice-select`, so no Check fails. The reject is for a clear miss of the bar:

bar, Rail list inset: at the default 288 px Rail the head raises the compact breakpoint from `@container rail (width <= 252px)` to `(width <= 288px)`, which sets the list's padding-inline to 0 and hides its scrollbar. On tree-40 at 1280 the rows start at x 0 (main: x 16), and the overflowing list shows no scrollbar. U172's "the Rail list keeps its leading --space-4 inset" no longer holds at the default width, so the whole Rail changes to make room for one control. Fix: keep the 252px breakpoint and fit the split add inside the row instead, for example by collapsing the `Agent` label at the default width as the ≤252px rule already does.
bar, focused Workstream row: with the row flush against the Rail's edges under `overflow-x: clip`, the focus ring shows only its top and bottom edges, and the name is cut to `aut…` (tree-40 1280 dark, `auth-refactor` focused; main shows `auth-r…` inside a full ring). Restoring the inset as above restores the ring.

NOTE: the `▾` half is a text glyph next to 16 px icon marks; a chevron Icon would match the row.
NOTE: the picker itself (labelled selects on --ground, quiet `Add agent`, long labels cut inside the select) is a clear improvement on main's unstyled selects.

Report: artifacts/ux/U378/report.md.

Reviewed-by-Agent: critic-38391848128): Merge remote-tracking branch 'origin/main' into build/issue-1253; U172 assert split add preserves default Rail inset; U378 fit split add without removing the default Rail inset

bar, Rail list inset: met. The compact breakpoint is back to `width <= 252px`. At the default 288 px Rail the list keeps its 16 px inset and its scrollbar, and the `Agent` label collapses instead.
bar, focused Workstream row: the focus ring is met. On tree-40 at 1280 dark, focused `backend` and `auth-refactor` each show a full ring inside the list. The name part remains a finding (below).

bar, third-level Workstream row actions, tree-40 1280 dark at the default 288 px Rail, with a Workstream `schema-migration` nested under `auth-refactor` (fake `rail.tree` adds it) and focused:
Seen: the row's actions end at x 280, past the row's right edge at x 272. `Open in editor` is cut off, a horizontal scrollbar appears across the Rail list, and the name shrinks to its 16 px floor (`s…`). Main fits exactly (actions end at x 272) and has no horizontal scrollbar. This breaks U378's "no … button overflows or is clipped".
Change that would meet it: at the default width, give the actions no more room than main's five buttons. For example, extend the existing `.rail-row[aria-expanded] .row-icons > [aria-label="Open folder"]` hide rule from `width < 220px` to `width <= 288px`.
Then add a focused depth-3 Workstream row to `u378_the_split_add_renders_without_overflow`.
bar, focused nested Workstream name, tree-40 1280 dark, `auth-refactor` focused:
Seen: the name is cut to `au…` (36 px wide); main shows `auth-r…` (60 px).
Change that would meet it: the same fix as above returns the 24 px.

Delta (head vs main, tree-40 1280 dark):
`backend` focused: name 64 px vs 88 px; padding-inline-start 16 px on both; 6 action buttons vs 5.
`auth-refactor` focused: name 36 px vs 60 px.
Depth-3 Workstream focused: actions' right edge 280 vs 272 (row edge 272); Rail list horizontal overflow true vs false.

NOTE: the `▾` half is still a text glyph next to 16 px icon marks; a chevron Icon would match the row.
NOTE: the open picker (labelled Model and Effort selects on --ground, long labels cut inside the select, a quiet `Add agent`) stays clean in light and dark.

Reviewed-by-Agent: critic-38399676332): Merge remote-tracking branch 'origin/main' into build/issue-1253; U378 guard focused nested Workstream action bounds; U378 fit focused Workstream actions at the default Rail width; U378 capture focused rows and check compact action tab order
- `review` (review rejected: REJECT: `7788818d` changes `@container rail (width < 220px)` to `(width <= 288px)` in `apps/desktop/src/rail/styles.css`. That rule is `.rail-row[aria-expanded] .row-icons > [aria-label="Open folder"] { display: none; }`. The default Rail is 288px and the minimum is 252px (U389). So the old `< 220px` rule could never fire. The new rule hides `Open folder` on every Workstream row at the default width and at every narrower one.
- U427 (`scenarios/ui-rail-actions.md:16`) decides the Workstream row shows add an Agent, clear, open folder and open in editor. U426's Keyboard clause says every U427 icon is reached by Tab.
- U378 (`scenarios/models.md:38`) says "U426's row height, name layout and visibility rules still hold". It authorizes the split add only. It does not authorize dropping `Open folder`.
- To make that pass, `b5d4e50a` weakens `u426_every_icon_is_reached_by_tab_and_enter_or_space_runs_without_selecting`. On `main` it expects `Open folder` in the Tab order and runs it with Space. The head makes both conditional on `railWidth > 288`, so 288 never checks the icon. `u426_the_long_name_163` and the similar U426 test also edit the expected labels.
- Because the jsdom `u427_open_folder_*` tests do not apply container queries, CI stays green while the feature is gone at the default width.

Fix: keep `Open folder` at 288px. Fit the split add and the other actions another way, for example by dropping the split add's label sooner or tightening the icon gaps. Alternatively, have the Issue or scenario amend U427 and U426 to drop `Open folder` at ≤288px, and restore the U426 test to expect it until that amendment is on `main`.

NOTE: Earlier approvals covered `32415fdc` and `661053b7`. This head adds only the commits above plus merges of `main`. I did not rerun `just check` or the Chromium observer.
NOTE: Carried over: `--hover` is not in `tokens.css`. The `project.get` failure leaves `Add agent` disabled.

<!-- fix-exhausted #1453 -->
PR #1453 (https://github.com/saadshahd/roundup/pull/1453) used its 3 fix runs and was closed unmerged; its diff stays at that link, head `706fdb099b6d3e1bf3cd27492ac764a1381796e1`. Each line is a cause a fix run answered, its failing check or review finding, and the commits it pushed; the last is the cause that found no run left.

- `check` (check failed): A35, L84: install the check browser and settle the Rail before refusal
- `critic` (critic rejected: Captures: the tree-40 seed at 1280x800, light and dark, on head 315392b8 and origin/main. Two Checkpoints were sent by `checkpoint.written`: one with a titled `rows` Block, one with a `text` Block. I opened the log ("All messages") and walked plan → files → pending → result → failure. On main, every seed passes every check: agents-10, tree-40 dark, first-run dark, thread-report and decisions. On head, those seeds also pass every check when no Checkpoint is shown. This is the first critic run on this PR, so there are no earlier findings to re-check.

Delta: D2 goes from pass on main to fail on head; D10 goes from pass to fail because D2 fails. The failure is the same in light and dark.

rule D2, scenario U374, step plan, `h4.thread-checkpoint-block-title` keeps the browser's default margin (margin-top 15.96px), which is not a space step. It happens whenever a Block has a `title` (the PR's own capture uses `blocks: []`, so it never draws one). It leaves an uneven ~16px gap above and below "Decided" on the card. Reset the margin to 0, or to a space step, in `.thread-checkpoint-block-title`.
bar, rewind prompt, opens with its controls below the fold: on the last Checkpoint only "files changed after this" and half a path show above the composer. The radios, `rewind` and the auto-focused `keep` sit under the feed's bottom edge (elementFromPoint misses them) until the user scrolls the feed by hand. Scroll the prompt into view when it opens (for example `scrollIntoView({block: "nearest"})` on the prompt, or focus with scrolling), so the whole question and its answers are on screen together.
bar, rewind prompt agent lines, a long name wraps and its state word drops onto the next line. "back" then sits directly above "reviewer" and reads as a heading for the next Agent, and "under takeover" + "rewind it too" float under a three-line name with nothing tying them to it. Keep the state word on the name's line: let the name ellipsize or wrap inside its own span with the state word and checkbox fixed after it (for example a grid of `minmax(0,1fr) auto`), so each line reads `<name>  back` as U374 writes it.
bar, rewind prompt `rewind` button while it cannot act (no files choice yet) and while pending, still drawn in full `--accent` with a pointer cursor. `docs/design-system.md` (button states, l.87–91) says a disabled button uses `--disabled` text, cursor `default`, `aria-disabled="true"` and never the `disabled` attribute. Use `aria-disabled` plus a guard in the handler for `rewind`, `keep` and the inputs, so the user can see `rewind` is not yet available and that a rewind is in progress.
bar, files list, a three-line nested scroll box with a native scrollbar inside the popover, which is itself inside the scrolling feed. Paths are broken mid-word ("path-path-…-path-/path-path-path-0.tsx"), the third path is cut in half, and `+2 more` is hidden inside the inner scroll. Show at most 5 paths one per line, each ellipsized in the middle or start and with its full path as `title`, then `+<n> more`, with no inner scroll region.
NOTE: the popover (`position:absolute; top:100%`, `--ground`) covers the next Checkpoint card completely while open. This meets U46, but a hairline-only box over live content reads heavier than an in-flow disclosure would.
NOTE: `styles.css` adds rules for `.thread-needs`, `.thread-checkpoints`, `.thread-checkpoints-empty` and `.thread-log > summary`, which nothing in this diff renders (U422 removed them from the view). These are dead selectors.
NOTE: Checkpoints render oldest first inside the log; U355 said newest first, though U422 took them out of the view.

Reviewed-by-Agent: critic-38403533842): Merge remote-tracking branch 'origin/main' into build/issue-808; U374 keep Rewind choices visible and readable; A35 wait for queued turns before checking Mark copies; U374 make scroll dependencies explicit
- `unfinished` (unfinished failed): Merge remote-tracking branch 'origin/main' into build/issue-808; U374 refresh Rewind captures after main merge
- `critic` (critic rejected: What I captured: tree-40 at 1280x800, light and dark, using the U374 flow (rows and text Blocks, then plan → files → pending → result → failure). I compared the PR's captures with my own harness runs on head. I also ran `__checks()` on head for agents-10, tree-40, first-run, thread-report and decisions in light and dark: D1–D14 all pass. The 20 U374 capture checks.json files (1280 and 1440, light and dark) also pass every Check.

Delta: none. Nothing that passes on main fails on head, and the earlier D2 failure now passes.

Earlier findings:
rule D2, `.thread-checkpoint-block-title` margin: fixed. It now has `margin: 0`, and "Decided" sits evenly on the card.
bar, rewind prompt opening below the fold: fixed. The prompt calls `scrollIntoView({block:"nearest"})` when it opens. In plan, files, pending and failure, every control is visible above the composer.
bar, a long Agent name pushing the state word onto the next line: fixed. The row is a grid of `minmax(0,1fr) auto auto` and the name ellipsizes, so each line reads `<name> back` or `<name> under takeover [ ] rewind it too`.
bar, `rewind` drawn as enabled while unavailable or pending: fixed. It uses `aria-disabled`, `--disabled`, cursor `default` and a guard in the handler. `keep` and the inputs do the same, and `rewind` has a reason as its `title`.
bar, files list as a nested scroll box: fixed. At most five paths show, one per line, ellipsized at the start and with the full path as `title`, then `+n more`, with no inner scroll region. But the way it ellipsizes causes the new finding below.

Findings on head:
bar, rewind prompt files list, a path that starts or ends with a neutral character is reordered by `<bdi dir="rtl">{path}</bdi>`: in the harness, `.github/workflows/build.yml` draws as `github/workflows/build.yml.` and `.agents/data/harness.md` draws as `agents/data/harness.md.` (a leading `_` moves to the end the same way). A path the user must judge before choosing "chats and files" reads as a different file. Fix: put `dir="rtl"` on the ellipsizing block (the `li` or a wrapper), keep the path in an inner `<bdi dir="ltr">`, and keep `text-align: left`. The ellipsis then stays at the start and the characters stay in order; I checked this in Chromium.

NOTE: an Agent row with a short name (for example "ws") places its state word at the far right of the prompt, about 290px away, because the name column is `1fr`. `minmax(0, max-content) auto auto` would keep `<name>  back` together and still ellipsize long names.
NOTE: in the failure capture (card about 336px wide), the card header wraps and the `rewind` word drops onto a line of its own with a slight indent. This happens because the card shrinks to fit the prompt. A `flex-wrap: nowrap` header with the title ellipsizing, or a card that fills the column width, would keep it on one line.
NOTE: the paths start about 5px to the right of "files changed after this" and the other text in the prompt.
